counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of malignancy was found on re-review of hysterectomy/oophorectomy specimens, so the original surgery was not independently diagnostic of carcinoma
SMA, desmin, and myogenin negativity rules out a smooth-muscle explanation such as leiomyomatosis peritonealis disseminata
Endometriosis was present and cauterized, but no malignant transformation of endometriosis is reported to make endometriosis the diagnostic entity
decisive_items: A vaginal biopsy showed grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma
A core-needle biopsy of a 9 cm left pelvic mass revealed poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
response.rationale: The champion is the only candidate directly confirmed by histology as a specific malignant subtype: grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The poorly differentiated epithelioid pelvic mass and multifocal abdominal/thoracic masses are compatible with metastatic/disseminated carcinoma. The runner-up captures the plausible iatrogenic morcellation-dispersion mechanism, but it is not the tumor diagnosis itself. Endometriosis and leiomyomatosis peritonealis disseminata are excluded by the carcinomatous morphology and negative smooth-muscle panel; R6 is too nonspecific compared with the vaginal biopsy diagnosis.

rejected.why: Endometriosis was incidental and cauterized; it cannot explain the grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma or widespread hypermetabolic masses.
Leiomyomatosis peritonealis disseminata is excluded by the present epitheloid carcinomatous morphology and by negative SMA, desmin, myogenin, and other smooth/muscle markers.
Poorly differentiated carcinoma captures the morphology but is less specific than the definitive vaginal-biopsy diagnosis of grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
